newsitem.title: USA: Union spokesman quickly sounds pessimistic tone.
newsitem.headline: Union spokesman quickly sounds pessimistic tone.

text.p: Allied Pilots Association spokesman David Bates quickly reversed his faintly optimistic remarks Friday about talks with American Airlines, saying he was not hopeful of an agreement tonight.

"We're not optimistic that we're going to reach an agreement tonight," Bates said, only a short while after saying there were "some glimmers of hope" in talks aimed at averting a strike at midnight (0500 GMT Saturday).
The union's chief negotiator Brian Mayhew called the progress "fairly minimal" and "somewhat disappointing."
"We're closer now than when we started, but we are still really far apart," he told reporters.
Bates' earlier hint of optimism contrasted sharply with comments earlier in the day by union president James Sovich who described the negotiations as "slow and difficult."
Meanwhile, the union's board has started meeting away from the site of negotiations.
The board was expected to give Sovich the authority to declare a strike if the talks with American fail.

Fort Worth, Texas-based American carries about 20 percent of the nation's air travelers. If the airline shuts down it is expected to strand thousands of passengers and could cost the economy up to $200 million a day.
